statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks have one conclusive outcome. Five representative surfaces were inspected; authenticated, write/post, comment submission and destructive account actions were not exercised because they require credentials or mutate live community data.

page.framework: Legacy server-rendered HTML with jQuery and Swiper; some feed modules injected client-side
page.notes: The mobile homepage links to a mini-gallery route that redirected to the desktop gall.dcinside.com template in the tested browser. Coverage excludes authenticated settings, posting, commenting, moderation, and checkout because they require credentials or alter live data.

paths.description: Mobile homepage and primary discovery/search surface; represents the entry template and content feed.
A prominent live mini-gallery reached from the homepage; represents listing/community navigation. It redirected to a desktop gall.dcinside.com listing.
A live article link selected from the gallery listing; represents detail navigation and the not-found recovery state.
All-services/settings surface; represents navigation, preferences and custom controls.
Authentication form reached from the homepage; represents the primary account flow.

findings.summary: Dark preference does not activate the available night theme
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually the same light theme as the default screenshot; the settings page exposes a separate manual night-mode toggle.
findings.suggestedFix: Connect the night palette to prefers-color-scheme and declare color-scheme, while retaining the explicit override.

findings.summary: Route and state changes use abrupt legacy navigation
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found zero view-transition usage across the homepage, while gallery navigation performs a full redirect to a different desktop surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful navigation changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Carousel and disclosure interactions rely on legacy scripted controls
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM includes Swiper and JavaScript-driven menus, while the probe found no scroll-snap or native disclosure primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer scroll snap/overscroll and semantic controls for gesture surfaces; keep scripting as enhancement.

findings.summary: Long feeds provide no scroll-state-aware orientation
findings.evidence: The 2,456px homepage has no scroll-state query or progress treatment in the DOM/CSS probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scroll-aware header or progress/back-to-top affordance where it improves orientation.

findings.summary: A primary gallery route breaks mobile visual continuity
findings.evidence: Following a prominent mobile mini-gallery link redirects to a desktop listing rendered as tiny, unreadable content at 390px.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the mobile template and current-location context across gallery navigation.

findings.summary: Settings and overlays use custom div/label controls instead of semantic primitives
findings.evidence: The settings DOM contains custom label-based switches and full custom layer popups; the homepage probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native dialog/popover/details and real checkbox/switch controls with names, states and keyboard behavior.

findings.summary: The entry view is dense with competing navigation and feed chrome
findings.evidence: The first mobile viewport contains search, recent-gallery, four primary tabs, ranking controls, four feed tabs, carousel controls and multiple content modules before a stable reading hierarchy emerges.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce competing chrome and make one primary content/navigation hierarchy dominant.

findings.summary: A mobile route falls back to a desktop-width template
findings.evidence: The selected gallery route redirects to gall.dcinside.com and its entire desktop page is shrunk into the 390px capture; the probe found no container-query usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a genuine mobile listing and use component-level responsive rules rather than shrinking a desktop canvas.

findings.summary: Many mobile controls are below recommended target size
findings.evidence: The active probe found many 20-38px controls; Lighthouse failed target-size, including 17px-high footer links. Keyboard focus was visible, but touch sizing is not adequate.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase actionable areas and spacing to at least the guidance/WCAG target baseline without reducing visible focus.

findings.summary: Homepage-to-gallery navigation does not preserve a usable mobile flow
findings.evidence: A prominent homepage gallery choice ends on a desktop listing whose content is illegibly scaled at the tested mobile viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep listing and detail journeys on responsive templates with stable URLs and predictable back navigation.

findings.summary: Initial loading is slow
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 11.0s LCP, 9.4s FCP and 18.0s time to interactive; the independent trace measured 4.11s LCP. Both exceed good-range loading targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP path, reduce blocking CSS/JS and defer non-critical feeds and analytics.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and uncompressed resources delay content
findings.evidence: HAR recorded seven parser-blocking stylesheets and synchronous parser scripts; six CSS files over 2KB were uncompressed, including 373KB contents.css.
findings.suggestedFix: Compress and split CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, and shorten the critical dependency chain.

findings.summary: The page ships large amounts of unused CSS and JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 787KiB unused CSS and 293KiB unused JavaScript; three separate gtag bundles each transfer about 163-165KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicated analytics loads and deliver route/component-scoped CSS and JS.

findings.summary: Core controls and content lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name, frame-title and image-alt; the probe also found one visible unlabeled search input.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control an accessible name, label search inputs, title frames, and provide meaningful or empty alt text as appropriate.

findings.summary: Several text colors fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.26:1 green ranking text and 2.03-2.14:1 orange tab text where 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG contrast in every theme and state.

findings.summary: Document structure is incomplete and heading order skips levels
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark and a non-sequential heading order. Focus is visible, but the structural defects impair assistive navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark and repair heading hierarchy while preserving the native visible focus outline.

findings.summary: Gallery content becomes illegibly small on mobile
findings.evidence: The 390px gallery screenshot shows an entire desktop layout compressed into a narrow viewport, making labels and post rows unreadable without zoom.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a mobile reading layout with fluid type and one-column content rather than scaling a desktop page.

findings.summary: Zoom is constrained and touch targets are undersized
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because maximum-scale is 2 and failed target-size; the DOM confirms the restrictive viewport metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow unrestricted user zoom (or at least 5x) and enlarge/space controls.

findings.summary: Image sizing and aspect-ratio handling are unsound
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 100 images without width/height and Lighthouse enumerated distorted image aspect ratios.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions/aspect-ratio and use object-fit only where deliberate cropping is intended.

findings.summary: A third-party script uses a deprecated browser API
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported the deprecated Topics API in t1.kakaocdn.net/kas/static/ba.min.js and failed inspector-issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or remove the affected ad dependency and retest DevTools Issues.

findings.summary: Rendered content and links depend heavily on JavaScript
findings.evidence: The raw-vs-rendered check found only 19% content coverage without JavaScript, and the DOM probe counted 944 of 1,162 anchors with empty or javascript-style hrefs.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful feed/link content and use real href URLs, progressively enhancing interaction.

findings.summary: Sitemap/indexing signals are incomplete
findings.evidence: robots.txt is available, but /sitemap.xml returned the site not-found HTML; the mobile canonical points broadly to the desktop homepage instead of preserving the mobile URL relationship.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid sitemap and use page-specific canonical signals consistently across templates.

findings.summary: The organization/home entity lacks structured data
findings.evidence: Open Graph/Twitter metadata exists, but the live probe found zero JSON-LD blocks for the site/organization entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate WebSite/Organization JSON-LD aligned with visible content and existing social metadata.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but defensive headers and cookie attributes are weak
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; 14 cookies were observed and 14 were flagged insecure, with most lacking Secure and using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP, HSTS and nosniff, then mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite/HttpOnly policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party transfer are disproportionate
findings.evidence: Tracker inspection found five known tracker domains. HAR attributed 55 of 64 requests and 2.11MB of 2.30MB to non-main origins, including three gtag bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit and consolidate analytics, obtain appropriate consent, minimise identifiers/events, and defer non-essential third parties.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks modern credential assistance
findings.evidence: The login DOM contains code and password fields without autocomplete tokens; no WebAuthn/passkey use was detected. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct username/current-password autocomplete and offer passkey/WebAuthn authentication.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing HSTS/CSP; the page declares an unsafe-url meta referrer policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, strict referrer and permissions policies, and evaluate Trusted Types/origin isolation for the script-heavy surface.

findings.summary: Most feed content disappears without JavaScript
findings.evidence: The discoverability primitive found only 19% rendered-content coverage in raw HTML; the crawler screenshot contains placeholders rather than article text.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core listings and links, then progressively enhance carousels, ranking and personalization.

findings.summary: Custom overlays and desktop redirects make runtime behavior brittle
findings.evidence: The settings DOM uses custom popup layers and JavaScript hrefs, while gallery navigation switches to a desktop template rather than adapting in place.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native top-layer primitives and stable responsive routes; retain state through navigation and DOM changes.

findings.summary: The login form does not expose robust native validation semantics
findings.evidence: Login inputs have labels but no required constraints or described error regions in the DOM; custom JavaScript owns submission feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints, validate after interaction, and connect clear errors with aria-invalid/aria-describedby and a live summary.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete tokens
findings.evidence: The login DOM shows code and password inputs with no autocomplete values, preventing reliable credential-manager assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use stable names and appropriate username/current-password autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Images are not responsively or dimensionally optimized
findings.evidence: The image audit found 17 oversized images, 100 without dimensions and almost no srcset use.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive image candidates at display-appropriate sizes and include intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Duplicated analytics and unused code create avoidable work
findings.evidence: Three gtag bundles transfer roughly 491KB total; Lighthouse estimated 293KiB unused JS and 787KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics and conditionally load only code needed for the current surface.

findings.summary: Third-party cost dominates the page budget
findings.evidence: HAR measured 2.11MB third-party transfer out of 2.30MB total and tracker inspection found 12 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove duplicate trackers and defer ads/analytics until they provide user value or consent exists.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is high for a mobile content index
findings.evidence: The heap summary contained about 418k nodes and 25.8MB self size. Repeated menu/scroll interaction grew only ~0.8%, but the baseline object population is substantial.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicated DOM/carousel clones and unnecessary third-party runtime state; profile constructor populations after cleanup.

taskList.title: Restore a coherent responsive mobile gallery and article journey
Fix accessible names, semantics, contrast, zoom and touch targets
Cut the critical path and remove duplicate analytics/CSS
Deploy defensive headers and secure cookie attributes
Minimise tracking and enforce a third-party budget
Server-render core feed content and real links
Use semantic native overlays and controls
Connect dark mode to system preference
Correct image sizing and responsive delivery
Modernise login assistance, validation and passkeys
